headlines.article_text: SpaceX agrees to testify to NYC Council about AI safety Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points SpaceX has agreed to testify before the New York City Council as part of an investigation into artificial intelligence safety risks. The city council subpoenaed SpaceX CEO Elon Musk ordering that he or another representative testify at a hearing last week. SpaceX skipped that hearing, while representatives from Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta and Google all testified. In this article SPCX Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT SpaceX CEO Elon Musk attends a meeting with US President Donald Trump and technology executives about artificial intelligence in the East Room of the White House in Washington, DC, on Sept. 29, 2026. Kent Nishimura | AFP | Getty Images SpaceX has agreed to testify before the New York City Council this week as part of a legislative investigation concerning artificial intelligence safety risks, the council announced on Tuesday. The council said in a press release that the hearing will take place on Friday at 10 a.m. ET in front of its tech committee. Julie Menin, council speaker, and Nwamaka Ejebe, general counsel, issued a subpoena to Elon Musk and SpaceX's AI unit on Sept. 28, compelling testimony for a hearing that took place last week. Representatives from Anthropic , OpenAI , Google and Meta all testified at the hearing on Oct. 5, but SpaceX did not appear. Menin said in Tuesday's statement that SpaceX agreed two days later to testify after the council said it intended to have its subpoena enforced by a judge. "Last Monday, we held a major, hours-long hearing with whistleblowers, the world's largest tech companies, and the nation's foremost experts in AI," Menin said in Tuesday's release. "Conspicuously absent was SpaceXAI, which is unacceptable." Musk folded his AI venture, xAI, into SpaceX in February, creating a conglomerate that includes its Grok models, which are used by some federal agencies, including the Pentagon . SpaceX went public in June and is now valued at over $2 trillion. In August, SpaceX also completed a $60 billion acquisition of AI coding startup Cursor. SpaceX competes with Anthropic and OpenAI in the AI market, though Grok trails far behind models from top rivals. The NYC council opened its investigation following a month of intense debate surrounding the risks posed by advanced AI models. In its original letter ordering testimony from Musk or another SpaceX leader, the council said its investigation would help, "assess whether fast-emerging risks to public safety, cybersecurity, economic stability, privacy, consumers and businesses warrant immediate legislative action to protect New Yorkers." SpaceX's "failure to comply" with the subpoena, the council warned, could subject the company to penalties or other punishment under New York City laws and regulations. Carmen De La Rosa, chair of the tech committee, told CNBC in a statement that the council expects answers from SpaceX. "With the proliferation of Elon Musk's technology at the federal level, it is even more important they come to the discussion with robust context about data privacy, safeguards, and whistleblower protections," she said. Lawsuits are piling up against SpaceX after Grok's image generator enabled mass production and distribution of deepfake porn based on images of real people who did consent. SpaceX didn't respond to a request for comment. — CNBC's Ashley Capoot contributed reporting. headlines.article_text: Visa gets Beijing's green light for bank card business after 40 years of working with China Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Visa said Tuesday it received China's approval to begin the process of establishing a local bank card clearing business. Mastercard and American Express have already gotten the approvals in the last several years. Visa's CEO became chair of the U.S.-China Business Council in June. In this article V Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Dado Ruvic | Reuters BEIJING — U.S. credit card giant Visa announced Tuesday it had received approval from the People's Bank of China for setting up a bank card clearing business in the country. The news comes as the U.S. and Chinese presidents plan for their third meeting this year. "This marks an important milestone toward the company serving China's domestic payments market," Visa said in a statement. "For more than 40 years, Visa has been an active contributor to China's dynamic payments landscape," Visa CEO Ryan McInerney said. "We look forward to taking the necessary steps in the process, pursuant to the PBOC's regulations, to begin operating domestically in China." McInerney joined U.S. President Donald Trump's business delegation to Beijing in May and subsequently became chair of the U.S.-China Business Council in June. The Visa CEO also led a trip to Beijing in early September . "The timing is notable," said George Chen, partner and chair of digital practice, The Asia Group. "Beijing chose to approve visa's license just ahead of the APEC Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen next month, where Xi [Jinping] and Trump are expected to meet again," he said. "The move suggests that Beijing is keen to demonstrate tangible progress for American businesses before Trump's next visit to China." Trump told Fox News after his Beijing trip in May that he brought up Visa's request to gain China market access.
